title: The Bounce Is a Trap. Cem Karsan Says the Opex Floor Comes Off Friday.
speaker: Cem Karsan (Kai Volatility), guest

macro_themes.view: Structural vol selling and dealer delta buyback around expiration make it hard for markets to fall; the support rolls off after OpEx, opening a 'window of weakness'.
A contested midterm outcome is underpriced; event vol is priced at the election date rather than behind it, so Dec-Feb vol looks cheap.
Macro realities (bond market worries) are being masked short term by expiration flows but will eventually come through.

calls.condition: Weakness expected once OpEx vol compression and delta buyback roll off after Friday's expiration.
calls.reason: Expiration-week vol compression forces dealers to buy back deltas, creating mean-reverting bounces; once that rolls off, macro risks can assert themselves, as after Feb 2020 OpEx.
calls.quote: these windows of weakness and these issues tend to happen um coming out of expiration or towards the end of expiration

calls.reason: Vol compressed into OpEx; contested-midterm risk underpriced, so later-dated (Dec/Jan/Feb) vol is cheap relative to November.
calls.quote: I think you can get much cheaper December, January, February vol than you can in November

notes: Short-term ES bias is a judgment: he describes OpEx-supported bounces now and weakness coming out of expiration (title: 'bounce is a trap'); the 1-5 day horizon spans the post-OpEx period. Recorded during expiration week before Friday OpEx; exact day not stated.
